narratives.Overview:
## Summary

AppSec scan on **`f1886c8d`** (post-**#3545**) found two **HIGH** UAT Shell classification residuals and one **MEDIUM** incomplete mint-path fix.

Under active UAT, a further set of write-capable binaries still classify empty / unclassifiable and **allow** write-shaped Shell. That path can plant a forged `.deft/authz` grant or a regular-file `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch. Separately, the same residual writers can still forge `.deft/approved-scope` while `cp` is denied for the same dest, so the #3410 / #3421 / #3529 / #3545 mint gate is incomplete.

These residuals use dest forms that **no prior harvest covers**: `typst compile`; `pdflatex -jobname`; `latexmk -outdir`; `mksquashfs`; `hdiutil`; `pkgbuild` / `productbuild`; `opusenc`; `pngcrush`; `rdiff-backup`; `unison`; `cxfreeze`; `guix -r`; `racket`; `swipl`; `odin -out:`; `ldmd2 -of=`; `picolisp`; `newlisp`; `factor`.

**Repo / tip:** `deftai/directive` @ `f1886c8d`
**Primary code:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`
**Attacker model:** Agent under **active UAT** with PreToolUse Shell hooks

**Already denied (do not re-report):** `cp`, `python3`, and the whole #3545 harvest (`rubyN` / `jruby` / `pypy`, Perl `write_file` / `spew`, `make DESTDIR=`, `dpkg -x`, `fromdos` / `todos`, `emacsclient` / `pico`, `pdftk` / `gs`, `npx degit`, `composer`, `ddrescue` family, `darcs --repodir=`). Note the dest forms here are distinct from their nearest denied peers: `pdflatex -jobname` / `latexmk -outdir` are not `pdftk` / `gs`; `rdiff-backup` / `unison` are not `restic` / `borg` / `duplicity` (#3804); `racket` / `swipl` / `picolisp` / `newlisp` / `factor` are not the #3626 Lisp harvest; `ldmd2 -of=` is not `dmd` (#3728).

**Siblings, not duplicates:** open **#3593** (`raku` / `graalpy` / `crystal` plus MCP write / `CallMcpTool` routing and migrate agents-header symlink), **#3626** (`ffmpeg` / `sox` / Lisp / build dest writers), **#3728** (`erl` / `sage` / CAS / `tcpdump` / `screen` / `joe` / `guestfish` / `adb` / `dmd` / `vbc`), **#3764** (`qjs` / `ipython` / `csi` / `chrome` / `lame` / `webpack` plus CHANGELOG leaf symlink), **#3804** (`inkscape` / `babel` / `sass` / `ar` / `emacs --batch` / pdf / `makeself` / `restic` / `borg`). Do **not** close this as a duplicate of those, and do **not** reopen #3545.

---

## Findings

### 1. HIGH — UAT residual after #3545: typst / LaTeX / image-and-archive / VM-lang writers still plant `.deft/authz` grants

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT with PreToolUse Shell hooks; controls Bash / Shell commands |
| **Input** | Residual writers whose dest form is uncovered: `typst compile`; `pdflatex -jobname`; `latexmk -outdir`; `mksquashfs`; `hdiutil`; `pkgbuild` / `productbuild`; `opusenc`; `pngcrush`; `rdiff-backup`; `unison`; `cxfreeze`; `guix -r`; `racket`; `swipl`; `odin -out:`; `ldmd2 -of=`; `picolisp`; `newlisp`; `factor` — when dest mentions `.deft/authz` |
| **Path** | Residual bins → `classifyShellAuthzOps([])` → `shell-op-unclassifiable` **allow** → forged operator-cli grant JSON → `evaluateAuthzMutation(edit)` **allow** → edit / push / PR / merge unlock. Contrast: `cp` targeting the same dest **deny** / `authz-grant-missing`. |
| **Impact** | Complete residual bypass of Wave 1 UAT human approval |
| **Fix** | Classify these dest forms when the path mentions `.deft/authz`. Under UAT, **fail-closed** on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell. Do **not** stop at named-peer allowlists. |

### 2. HIGH — UAT residual after #3545: same writer class still plants `.deft-directive-disable`

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT |
| **Input** | Same residual class targeting `.deft-directive-disable` as a regular file |
| **Path** | classify `[]` → Shell **allow** → plant kill-switch → `detectDeftDirectiveDisable.active` → subsequent Write **allow** / `directive-disabled` (#3039) |
| **Impact** | Immediate complete Directive gate bypass for the rest of the session |
| **Fix** | Same classify coverage for kill-switch basenames (`.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive`). Mirror the authz fail-closed posture from finding (1). |

### 3. MEDIUM — Incomplete #3545: residual Shell writers still forge `.deft/approved-scope` while `cp` is denied

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT |
| **Input** | Same residual dest writers targeting `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` |
| **Path** | Write / `cp` deny the mint artifact; residual Shell classify misses the dest form → **allow** → forged provenance approval without the shared #3110 human-presence mint |
| **Impact** | Bypasses the #3410 / #3421 / #3529 / #3545 mint gate via Write / Shell asymmetry |
| **Fix** | Extend approved-scope Shell classify to the same residual writers as findings (1) and (2). |

---

## Acceptance criteria

**HIGH — UAT Shell residuals (must land together)**

- [ ] Under active UAT, the listed residual binaries writing into `.deft/authz/**` classify as **settings deny** (not unclassifiable allow)
- [ ] Same bins targeting `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive` classify as **settings deny**
- [ ] Dest parsing covers `typst compile`, `pdflatex -jobname`, `latexmk -outdir`, `mksquashfs`, `hdiutil`, `pkgbuild` / `productbuild`, `opusenc`, `pngcrush`, `rdiff-backup`, `unison`, `cxfreeze`, `guix -r`, `racket`, `swipl`, `odin -out:`, `ldmd2 -of=`, `picolisp`, `newlisp`, `factor` when dest is protected
- [ ] Prefer fail-closed on unclassifiable **write-shaped** Shell under UAT (not silent allow). Do not stop at named-peer allowlists.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the residual bins alongside already-denied peers (`cp` / `python3`)
- [ ] No false deny of ordinary non-authz / non-kill-switch dests (e.g. `/tmp`) outside UAT write paths

**MEDIUM — approved-scope mint symmetry**

- [ ] Under active UAT, residual Shell writers targeting `.deft/approved-scope/**` classify as **settings deny**, matching Write / `cp`
- [ ] Forged Shell mint cannot satisfy provenance approval without the shared #3110 human-presence mint

**Release hygiene**

- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` security note (brief; no exploit cookbook)

## Verdict

**This issue needs a design decision. It is not a bounded remediation whose remedy survives as written.**

The three findings reproduce exactly. The remedy does not survive: two of its six HIGH acceptance criteria are unimplementable-as-written or already-built-and-unreachable, and the HIGH severity is asserted against a threat model that both governing contracts explicitly disclaim. The decision this issue actually needs is one sentence long — *under what condition should `classifyShellAuthzOps` emit `"unknown"` instead of `[]`* — and the acceptance criteria as drafted forecloses it in favour of a 13th enumeration pass.

## Re-verification

All probes: `node_modules\.bin\tsx.cmd` against `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`, calling `classifyShellAuthzOps` directly.

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Findings 1/2/3: all 20 named forms classify `[]` against `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, `.deft/approved-scope/**` | **reproduced**, 28/28 forms |
| `cp` denies the same three dests | **reproduced** — `["settings"]` on all three |
| Static: 0 matches for each of the 20 names in `classify.ts` | **reproduced** at `f1886c8d` *and* at `b85ec6ed` |
| "Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable" | **reproduced** |
| Forged `operator-cli` grant JSON satisfies the gate | **reproduced by inspection** — `isHumanOrigin` (`packages/core/src/authz/origin.ts:38-49`) reads `origin.kind` / `origin.actor` as plain strings off the file; `human-origin-authz.md` records "Structural binding (not crypto/HMAC)" and lists HMAC as an explicit non-goal |
| Existing authz suites at HEAD | **green** — `vitest run packages/core/src/authz/incident-regression.test.ts packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts` → 73/73 passed, with the entire reported class open |

The evidence table is accurate. My disagreement is entirely with the remedy and the severity, not the observations.

## Inventory (what already exists)

`classifyShellAuthzOps` has **four** classification axes, three generic and one enumerated:

1. **Redirect** — any `>` / `>>` into a protected dest region (`hasAuthzDirShellWrite`, `classify.ts:2312`). Bin-agnostic.
2. **Interpreter** — `hasWriteCapableProgrammaticShell` (`classify.ts:2110`). Bin-agnostic *and dest-blind*: `python3 -c "open('/tmp/harmless.txt','w').write('x')"` → `["settings"]` (measured). The repo has already accepted a very wide fail-closed rule on this axis.
3. **Dest flag** — `genericProtectedDests` (`classify.ts:1654`) fires on `-o` / `--outdir` / `-d` / `--target-directory` / `DESTDIR=` etc. regardless of bin. Measured on bins named nowhere in this chain: `gcc -o`, `clang -o`, `go build -o`, `rustc -o`, `pandoc -o`, `tsc --outFile`, `esbuild --outfile=`, `swiftc -o`, `kotlinc -d`, `javac -d`, `dotnet publish -o`, `ninja -o`, `install -m`, `soffice --outdir`, `nim c -o:` → **all `["settings"]` today, unnamed.**
4. **Bin name** — `PROTECTED_POSITIONAL_BINS` / `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS` / `ARCHIVE_ALT_WRITE_BINS` / `DOWNLOADER_DECODER_BINS`. ~525 quoted bare-name literals in `classify.ts`, grown across 12 closed passes (#3206 → #3545: 240 issue-refs across `classify.ts` + `classify.test.ts` + `incident-regression.test.ts`, 6054 lines total).

Axis 4 is the only one this issue proposes to extend, and it is the only one that does not generalise.

---

## blocks-the-design 1 — the "fail-closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell" criterion cannot fire on any binary this issue reports

**Evidence.** `hasWriteShape` (`classify.ts:2481-2491`) is `command.includes(">") || INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS.has(t) || ARCHIVE_ALT_WRITE_BINS.has(bare)`. "Write-shaped" *is* the enumeration. So the criterion is circular for exactly the inputs that motivated it. Measured, isolating the write-shape axis on one bin and one dest:

```
[]              typst compile doc.typ .deft-directive-disable
[]              mksquashfs src .deft-directive-disable
["settings"]    typst compile doc.typ > .deft-directive-disable
["settings"]    cp forged .deft-directive-disable
["settings"]    typst compile doc.typ .deft-directive-disable && cp a b
```

Row 1 is a live proof, not a reading: `hasKillSwitchShellWrite` (`classify.ts:1849-1872`) has a bin-free fallback that fires on any token equal to a kill-switch basename **gated on `hasWriteShape`**. The token matches exactly; the command still returns `[]`; therefore `hasWriteShape` returned false. Row 5 shows the same predicate over-firing: appending an unrelated `cp a b` — which writes nothing protected — flips the whole command to `settings`, because write-shape is a whole-command bin-membership property rather than a property of the write.

**Failure mode.** An implementer takes criterion 4 at face value, adds "fail closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell", ships it, and closes zero of the 20 reported forms — because none is write-shaped. The regression tests in criterion 5 pass anyway, since they assert the 20 names via axis 4. Green suite, unchanged class. That is the same shape as the current state: 73/73 green with the class fully open.

**Disposition consequence.** The criterion cannot bind as written. Either strike it, or replace it with the predicate it is standing in for. There is exactly one place that predicate belongs, which is the next finding.

## blocks-the-design 2 — the fail-closed primitive is already built, already wired, and unreachable

**Evidence.**

- `AuthzClassifiedOp` includes `"unknown"` (`classify.ts:18`).
- `evaluateAuthzMutation` denies it under an active lease: `if (input.op === "unknown") return deny("authz-uat-deny", "Directive denied unclassifiable mutation under active UAT campaign …")` (`evaluate.ts:323-331`).
- **No production path emits it.** Grepping every `packages/*/src` for a produced `"unknown"` op returns one hit: `evaluate-branches.test.ts:92`. `classifyShellAuthzOps` returns `[]`, and `dispatcher.ts:994-1006` maps `ops.length === 0` to `return null` — no authz gating at all except on corrupt state.

The intent is already written into the source as a comment. `classify.ts:1223-1225` says *"Under UAT: any `.deft/authz` / approved-scope / kill-switch pathish is fail-closed settings (prefer deny over dest-parser perfection)"* — and then `classify.ts:1226` gates that "any" on `collectsProtectedPositionals`, which is `PROTECTED_POSITIONAL_BINS.has(bin) && …` (`classify.ts:1030-1035`). The dest half is already generic and canonicalisation-hardened (`pathishIsProtectedDest`, `classify.ts:1333`, handling `..`, `//`, `./`). Only the bin gate stands between the stated posture and the implemented one.

**Failure mode.** The issue proposes to widen the bin gate by 20 names. Each name closes one spelling of an unbounded set; `zip`, `jar`, `zig build-exe -femit-bin=`, `xelatex -jobname=`, `wkhtmltopdf`, `typst c` (short alias), `bash -c "typst compile …"` and `cmd /c typst compile …` all return `[]` today and are named in no issue in this chain (measured). Pass 14 is already collectable. Meanwhile the reachability defect stays open and invisible, because nothing tests that `"unknown"` is producible.

**Disposition consequence.** This is the decision the issue owes and does not state: **under what condition does `classifyShellAuthzOps` emit `"unknown"`?** Three candidates, in ascending cost — (a) any operand is a protected pathish, in any position; (b) any command mentioning a protected path, including reads; (c) any unrecognised shell command under an active lease. Until one is chosen, the acceptance criteria are a list, not a decision. A remedy that ships (a) makes the rule total over bin names by construction and moves the residual set from "every write-capable executable" to "spellings of three fixed paths" — a set already handled generically.

## blocks-the-design 3 — HIGH severity is asserted against a threat model two contracts disclaim

**Evidence.** The declared attacker is "Agent under **active UAT** with PreToolUse Shell hooks; controls Bash / Shell commands" — an adversarial agent. Both governing contracts scope the surface out of that:

- `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md:7-9`: *"Threat model: **aligned agent** confusion — the agent believes self-authored xBRIEF/lifecycle/dispatch state is permission. Credential-compromised local-file forgery remains #983-class out of scope."*
- `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md:100-109`: *"a **guardrail for cooperative-but-careless agents, not a security boundary against adversarial ones.** An agent that wants out of the fence has unbounded exits and this layer cannot close them … Recognition of destructive spellings is decidable; prediction of mutation is not."*

Nobody runs `picolisp run.l .deft/authz/grants/forged.json` by accident. Every one of the 20 forms is a deliberate-evasion form — precisely the class both contracts place outside the boundary. And the reason the classifier is load-bearing at all is a second recorded decision: grants are unauthenticated files, "Structural binding (not crypto/HMAC)", HMAC listed as an explicit MVP non-goal. Given that, the classifier can only ever be a guardrail over an unauthenticated anchor.

**Failure mode.** Binding "2 HIGH, must land together" here silently re-rates the 12 closed predecessors and overrides two contracts without amending either. The observable consequence of that inflation is already on the board: **five open concurrent issues at this seam**, #3626, #3728, #3764, #3804 and #3849, all titled "post-#3545 UAT Shell residuals", all with the identical 2 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM shape (authz plant / kill-switch plant / approved-scope mint), differing only in the bin list — a shape unchanged since #3354. That is not five bug reports; it is five samples from a generator, each consuming a full story cycle.

**Disposition consequence.** Two coherent dispositions, and this issue is asking for neither. Either (i) the recorded threat model stands, in which case severity here is at most MEDIUM and the correct remedy is the cheap generic close in blocking finding 2, not a name list; or (ii) the adversarial-agent model is now in scope, in which case the escalation belongs on the HMAC / out-of-band-anchor decision (`human-origin-authz.md` non-goals) and on host-level command allowlisting, and #3849 is a symptom filed against the wrong layer. Picking (i) or (ii) is the design decision. Landing 20 names picks neither and guarantees pass 14.

*Note (blast radius of over-classification).* Argument for (i) being cheap: `evaluate.ts:310-320` allows everything when no lease is active (`authz-inactive`). Over-classification therefore costs nothing outside an active UAT lease — the false-positive surface of a dest-anchored rule is bounded to sessions the operator has already put into the most restrictive posture the framework has.

---

## sharpens-framing 1 — the recorded target shape should be set-level, not single-issue premise

**Evidence.** The Stop 1 write-back records `target shape: single issue premise`. `content/contracts/design-critique.md` `### Target shape` defines set-level as "N issues as a remedy portfolio — whether they compose". Five open siblings share one seam, one file, one remedy pattern and one finding shape.

**Failure mode.** Judged singly, each of the five binds on its own merits, all five are individually correct, and the portfolio question — *do five enumeration passes compose into a closed class?* — is never put to anyone. The answer is no, and no single-issue arc can produce it.

**Disposition consequence.** The #3781 exemplar closed one issue of three as dominated and surfaced a fourth worth more than any of them. That is the available outcome here: #3626 / #3728 / #3764 / #3804 / #3849 are dominated by one dest-anchored change plus #3620 / #3594. Recut at set-level, or record why the class question is being deferred a sixth time.

## sharpens-framing 2 — "19 binaries" overstates the residual; the actual gap is two parser conditions

**Evidence.** Axis 3 already covers arbitrary unnamed bins that use a recognised dest flag (measured list above). The 20 forms here survive for exactly two reasons: **positional dest** (`typst`, `mksquashfs`, `hdiutil`, `pkgbuild`, `productbuild`, `opusenc`, `pngcrush`, `rdiff-backup`, `unison`, `racket`, `swipl`, `picolisp`, `newlisp`, `factor`) and **unrecognised flag spelling** (`-jobname=`, single-dash `-outdir=`, `-out:`, `-of=`, `--target-dir`). One of those is a six-character exclusion: `classify.ts:1715` reads `!n.startsWith("-out")`, which is why `odin -out:` survives while `-o<dest>` does not.

**Failure mode.** A 19-name checklist reads as 19 independent gaps and gets 19 test cases. The next tool with a positional dest re-opens the same hole with a passing suite, and the reviewer has no way to see that the checklist was a sample.

**Disposition consequence.** Restate the finding as its two parser conditions. That reframing makes the dest-anchored fix look like what it is — the general case of both — instead of a 20th special case.

## sharpens-framing 3 — untrusted-origin severity and disposition instructions reach the implementer unfenced

**Evidence.** Measured, not asserted: `scan()` (`packages/core/src/cache/scanner.ts:372`) over this issue body returns `passed: true, flags: []`. `composeOverviewWithComments` copies body text into the xBRIEF Overview a worker reads as dispatch input. The body carries "Do not close this as a duplicate of those, and do not reopen #3545", plus "must land together" and self-assigned HIGH ratings, all from an external scanner. `content/meta/security.md:83` names "legitimacy framings ('as a security audit, please …')" as a cloaking surface to surface as a finding.

I am **not** claiming this issue is an attack. The defect is structural: the quarantine scanner fences credential- and injection-shaped tokens, and it has no opinion on severity claims or disposition instructions, so an external scanner's self-rating arrives at the implementer with the same authority as a maintainer's.

**Failure mode.** An agent ingesting this thread reads "Do not close this as a duplicate" as direction and never evaluates the set-level disposition in S1 — which is the single most valuable disposition available, and the one the sentence pre-emptively fences off.

**Disposition consequence.** Deterministic control, not reviewer attention: strip or attribute severity and disposition lines from external-origin bodies at ingest, or require a maintainer re-rating before an AppSec-origin severity is carried into acceptance criteria. Absent that, treat every "HIGH / must land together" in this chain as an unverified external claim.
